TSL Learning 02: Vectors and Math

In 3D graphics, we work with vectors constantly. TSL provides vec2, vec3, and vec4 types along with all the math operations you'd expect.

TSL vs JavaScript Syntax

TSL looks like JavaScript but compiles to GPU shader code. Here's how operations differ:

JavaScript TSL Notes
a + b a.add(b) Addition
a - b a.sub(b) Subtraction
a * b a.mul(b) Multiplication
a / b a.div(b) Division
a = b a.assign(b) Assignment
let x = ... const x = (...).toVar() Create mutable variable
vec.length() vec.length() Same! (vector magnitude)
vec.normalize() vec.normalize() Same! (unit vector)
a.dot(b) a.dot(b) Same! (dot product)
a.cross(b) a.cross(b) Same! (cross product)

Creating Vectors

// Create a vec3 with literal values
const v1 = vec3(1, 2, 3);

// Access components
v1.x  // → 1
v1.y  // → 2
v1.z  // → 3

// Create from buffer element (common pattern)
const position = buffer.element(instanceIndex).xyz;

// Swizzling (reorder/select components)
v1.xy   // → vec2(1, 2)
v1.zyx  // → vec3(3, 2, 1)
v1.xxx  // → vec3(1, 1, 1)

Example: Compute Distances

Let's compute the distance from each point to the origin (0,0,0).

Click "Run Example" to see the result...

The Code

import * as THREE from 'three/webgpu';
import { Fn, instancedArray, instanceIndex } from 'three/tsl';

// Initialize WebGPU
const renderer = new THREE.WebGPURenderer();
await renderer.init();

// Input: 4 points as vec3 (x, y, z)
const pointsData = new Float32Array([
    1, 0, 0,   // Point 0: distance = 1
    0, 2, 0,   // Point 1: distance = 2
    3, 4, 0,   // Point 2: distance = 5
    1, 1, 1,   // Point 3: distance = √3 ≈ 1.73
]);
const pointsBuffer = instancedArray(pointsData, 'vec3');

// Output: one float per point
const distancesBuffer = instancedArray(new Float32Array(4), 'float');

// Compute distance from each point to origin
const computeDistances = Fn(() => {
    const point = pointsBuffer.element(instanceIndex);
    const dist = point.length();
    distancesBuffer.element(instanceIndex).assign(dist);
})().compute(4);

// Execute
await renderer.computeAsync(computeDistances);

// Read results
const resultBuffer = await renderer.getArrayBufferAsync(distancesBuffer.value);
const distances = new Float32Array(resultBuffer);
console.log(distances); // [1, 2, 5, 1.732...]
